clue.text: Key game involving a drained Grimsby, struggling to get out of the box?

definitions.text: struggling to get out of the box?

indicators.note: involving says the game, together with the key, wraps round the next piece

parts.note: ESC is the Escape key on a keyboard
polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: drained means emptied of its insides, leaving only the first and last letters

parts.note: the outer letters of Grimsby

explanation.surface: A puzzle about an unfortunate fishing town, Grimsby, drained and trapped in some sort of contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' is a keyboard key, not a musical or door key; Grimsby is an English port town.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapology is the stage art of freeing oneself from restraints, such as a locked box, so the question mark signals a definition by example.

clue.text: Mystery sample of cream/gin/elderberry served up

indicators.note: served up says the hidden letters are read backwards
a sample of the drink is a small portion taken from inside the words, so the letters are hidden there

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A puzzling tasting of a cocktail of cream, gin and elderberry being offered.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Mystery sample' as the definition, but 'sample of' is the signal that the letters lie inside the words, leaving 'Mystery' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzle or riddle, a plain synonym for something baffling.

clue.text: Tone songstress used on track

parts.note: Cher is an American singer
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A singer's voice heard on a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tone' and 'track' suggest music; tone is a colour shade here.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry is a shade of bright red, so it names a colour tone.

clue.text: Hole with rubbish over floor containing stray dog

parts.note: a pit is a hole
bull is short for nonsense, rubbish

indicators.note: the floor word contains the stray word

parts.note: a tier is a level or floor
to err is to stray

explanation.surface: A hole with rubbish dumped above floorboards where a stray dog lurks.
explanation.definitionFit: The pit bull terrier is a muscular breed of fighting dog.

clue.text: LA woman embraces Scotsman

indicators.note: embraces means hugs, so the woman's name wraps around the Scotsman

parts.note: Louisa is a woman's name
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles woman hugs a man from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: LA looks like Los Angeles; it is also the postal abbreviation of a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: LA is the standard US postal abbreviation of the southern state named after Louis XIV.

clue.text: Finales of kung fu fights to relish

indicators.note: finales are endings, so take the last letter of each of the first three words

explanation.surface: The climactic martial-arts fights to savour at the end of a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto means enthusiasm and enjoyment, a synonym of relish as a noun.

clue.text: Record of settlement that ends quest in Sandwich

indicators.note: in places the end letter inside the sandwich word

parts.note: a sub is a long sandwich roll

indicators.note: the letter that ends a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of quest

explanation.surface: Sounds like a document marking the deal that concluded a search in the Kent town of Sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich, capitalised, wants to be the Kent town; it is just a sandwich, a SUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque stub is the counterfoil kept as a record of a payment made.

clue.text: Flier promoted the vacant position with channel

indicators.note: promoted, raised up, reads the pieces upwards in this down answer
vacant means emptied, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the outer letters of the
a job is a position
a rut is a channel or groove

explanation.surface: An airline employee promoted into the empty post along with a TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: TE, JOB and RUT, read from the bottom up, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbojet is a jet engine or aircraft powered by one, something that flies.

clue.text: Hose part of garden overlooking birches?

indicators.note: overlooking means above, placing the garden part first in this down answer

parts.note: a flower bed is part of a garden
to birch is to beat, and socks means hits hard

explanation.surface: A garden hose above silver birch trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' seems a garden hose; it is stockings, and birches are beatings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose is an old word for socks and stockings, and bedsocks are a kind of such legwear.

clue.text: Chris with lens recreated enthralling opening of David Lean film

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the rearranged letters hold the next piece
recreated means made again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of David
to lean is to list, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A man with a camera remakes a picture by director David Lean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'David Lean' reads as the British director, but only D comes from David, and Lean gives LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Schindler's List is Steven Spielberg's 1993 Holocaust drama, a feature picture.

clue.text: Pants fiancée Pat occasionally dropped

definitions.note: British slang: pants means rubbish or incompetent, used as an adjective

indicators.note: letters dropped every other time leave the alternate letters, here the even ones

explanation.surface: Pat, an engaged woman, stumbled and let something fall now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the odd letters of FIANCEEPAT and the even ones remain. In British slang 'pants' means poor or useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone hopelessly bad at something; the slang adjective is a synonym for clumsy incompetence.

clue.text: Open dry superior wine after common one

indicators.note: after puts the dry, superior wine following the common one

parts.note: 'un is the colloquial, common pronunciation of one, as in 'a good 'un'
sec is French for dry, used of wines
U stands for upper class, superior
red is a wine

explanation.surface: A wine list: a fine dry red preferred after a cheap ordinary one.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class usage, hence superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsecured means not fastened or locked, so a door left unsecured is open, a synonym.

clue.text: Corsican who enters bar for a peer

indicators.note: enters says the word for who goes inside the bar

parts.note: a Mars bar is a chocolate bar
Corsica is French, and qui is French for who

explanation.surface: Asking which Corsican walks into a bar on behalf of a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars is the brand of chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquis is a nobleman ranking above an earl, and every such nobleman is a peer of the realm.

clue.text: Oriental figurine's fine, I reckon, reviewing leg

parts.note: OK means fine
IMO is the texting shorthand for in my opinion, I reckon

indicators.note: reviewing, looking back, turns the leg word round

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone appraising a Japanese ornament, judging it fine after looking again at its leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: An okimono is a small Japanese decorative carving or statuette placed for display, an example of such ornamental figure.

clue.text: Lift cold, fat-free meat on top of that hot dish

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
lean meat has no fat
and means in addition, on top of that
jerk is a spicy Jamaican dish, as in jerk chicken

explanation.surface: A menu instruction: lighten up with cold lean meat, then a spicy dish besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meat' sits with fat-free in the surface but is only a link to the menu picture; LEAN alone gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The clean and jerk is an Olympic weightlifting event, a two-stage lift of the barbell overhead.

clue.text: Number of obsessive faces in Glastonbury event thus

parts.note: anal, short for anal-retentive, means obsessively fussy

indicators.note: faces are fronts, so take the first letter of each word

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: A song by a fanatic performed at the Glastonbury festival, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure or song; it is something that numbs. Glastonbury is a big English music festival.
explanation.definitionFit: An analgesic is a painkiller, which numbs pain, making it a numb-er.

clue.text: S Beds motor racing centre for tiros that's full of cones

parts.note: cots are small beds
F1 is Formula One motor racing, with the 1 read as I

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: middle letter of tiros

explanation.surface: A Bedfordshire motor-racing school for beginners laid out with traffic cones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'S Beds' suggests South Bedfordshire; it is S and COTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots fir, or Scots pine, is a conifer tree that bears many cones.

clue.text: Sausage served unwrapped left in clutches of pet

indicators.note: in the clutches of means held by, so the pet holds the other letters

parts.note: a cat is a pet

indicators.note: unwrapped strips off the outer letters

explanation.surface: A sausage dished up without its wrapper was left in the claws of the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervelat is a smoked pork sausage, a type of salami.

clue.text: Sweet engineers with vehicle providing buff on the exterior

indicators.note: the buff colour word sits on the outside, wrapping the rest

parts.note: camel is a buff, yellowish-brown colour
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Army mechanics with a car polishing its outer bodywork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buff' looks like polish, but it is the colour CAMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Creme caramel is a set custard dessert with caramel sauce, and a dessert is called a sweet in Britain.

clue.text: Whine about business acquiring green space?

indicators.note: about means round the outside of the business word
acquiring means taking in, so the whine word takes in the business word

parts.note: a mew is a whining cry, as of a cat
ado means fuss or business, as in much ado

explanation.surface: Complaining about a firm buying up a park.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a grassy field, an example of an open green area, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Comparatively mean doorman?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: more close, close meaning stingy
second meaning: one who closes, such as a door

explanation.walkthrough: Close means mean with money, so its comparative is meaner; a doorman, whimsically, is one who closes doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Close is a British word for miserly, and a closer is literally a person who shuts something.

clue.text: Restaurant's tax returns finally written in time

indicators.note: returns means the tax word goes back the other way

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

indicators.note: in places the final letter inside the time word

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter

parts.note: last letter of written

explanation.surface: A restaurant's tax returns were at last completed on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax returns' reads as paperwork; returns is the reversal signal on VAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek eating place, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Taking second left out of football club stadium

indicators.note: taking away the letters named
out of says they leave the club name

parts.note: Arsenal is a London football club

explanation.surface: A footballer leaves a club, departing from its ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a sports ground surrounded by seating, essentially a stadium.

clue.text: She wrote books with set length, maintaining appeal

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the set word holds the appeal

parts.note: to gel is to set, like a jelly
to ask is to appeal for something

explanation.surface: An author is said to have written books of a fixed length while keeping them attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth Gaskell was a Victorian novelist, author of Cranford and North and South.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Gaskell was a Victorian English novelist, so she is a woman who wrote books.

clue.text: Unreal property reduced by 50 per cent seen beyond river head

indicators.note: beyond puts the halved word after the river

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall

indicators.note: cut by half, so only the first two of its four letters remain

parts.note: the first half of seen
a ness is a headland, a head

explanation.surface: An estate agent's tale of a property, halved in value, seen past the river headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'property' wants to be real estate; here it means a quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Falseness is the quality of not being genuine, so an unreal attribute or property.

clue.text: Runner's test coming from work

indicators.note: the test word comes away from the work word, leaving the rest

parts.note: industry is hard work
a try is a test or attempt

explanation.surface: An athlete's trial arising from his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete; in crosswords it is often a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a great river of Pakistan, and a river runs, hence the crossword sense of runner.

clue.text: Hotel's legal documents picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: writs are legal documents

explanation.surface: A hotel's legal papers have been collected.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London's Piccadilly, an example of a grand establishment of that kind.

clue.text: Theocrat, given two weeks, knocked out religious publication

indicators.note: knocked out means battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for week, twice

explanation.surface: A religious ruler, given a fortnight, was beaten up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Watchtower is the magazine of the Jehovah's Witnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Watchtower is a magazine published by the Jehovah's Witnesses, so it is a periodical of a faith.
